S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in the health or behavior of a family member
patient_info.stressor: Marisol became the main organizer for her older sister’s medical appointments after a sudden decline in her sister’s health disrupted the family’s usual shared responsibilities. At first Marisol’s spreadsheet tracking and careful questioning helped everyone stay coordinated, but across 11 months her interpretations of missed calls, billing errors, and changed appointment times became fixed beliefs about others deliberately concealing information from her, despite repeated corrections from relatives and clinic staff. The conviction strained family meetings and began spilling into her supervisory style at work, where she increasingly treated routine administrative mistakes as connected to the same concern. She came to psychiatric care after her primary care physician, hearing the persistence and rigidity of these beliefs during a visit for stress-related support, recommended a specialist assessment.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Outside of dealing with my sister’s appointments and trying to get straight answers, I still keep my home in order, pay my bills, and do my job. People may think I’m too focused on this, but I’m not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: Family meetings have become tense, and at work I’ve had a few uncomfortable conversations because I’ve pressed people harder about routine mistakes than I used to. I’m still managing my responsibilities, but it has started to affect how people respond to me.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 11 months, since my sister’s health suddenly got worse and I had to start coordinating her care.
